title: TypeScript SDK: Union Hydrator and Compatibility Tooling for Streaming & Schema Interop
creator: Priya Nair
description: Problem: The TypeScript SDK has inconsistent runtime behavior when decoding discriminated unions from streaming responses or partial payloads. Existing helpers cover codegen and zod wrappers at build time but fail gracefully across: 1) incremental streaming chunks, 2) models that emit variant-less fallback blocks, and 3) JSON-schema interoperability for downstream validation/telemetry. Goal: ship a compact runtime 'union hydrator' library inside the SDK that 1) progressively accumulates partial streaming output and emits best-effort typed objects as soon as discriminators are available, 2) provides a stable surface for zod and JSON-schema adapters to validate/hint without forcing heavy build-time codegen, and 3) offers migration tooling for customers using hand-rolled discriminators. Non-functional: must be tree-shakeable, minimal bundle overhead, and support Node 18+ and Deno/Browser bundles.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes a `hydrateUnionStream` API that takes a streaming iterable of strings/blobs and yields typed values or partial markers
`hydrateUnionStream` integrates with existing streaming retry/backoff hooks so hydration survives transient network reconnects
Library ships zod adapter `zodUnionHint` that consumes partials and returns a union-safe Zod parse result without blocking streaming delivery
JSON-schema adapter `schemaAlias` provides a stable mapping table so server-side schemas can be associated with runtime union variants
Unit tests cover 95% of hydrator code paths including out-of-order discriminator emission, missing fields, and non-JSON tokens
Bundle size increase under 2KB gzipped for minimal SDK consumer when tree-shaken
Documentation page with three examples: basic union streaming, migration from handwritten discriminators, and server-side JSON-schema registration
tasks: Design hydrator runtime API and back-compat surface (RFC)
Implement streaming accumulator with efficient buffer management and incremental discriminator detection
Implement Zod adapter and JSON-schema alias registry
Wire into SDK streaming pipeline and retry hooks
Add integration tests with simulated partial responses and reconnects
Author docs, examples, and migration guide
Open PRs: core SDK integration, docs site, and types package
notes: Design constraint: avoid forcing users to import entire Zod at runtime; adapter should accept a thin parse shim to enable alternative validators
Trade-offs considered: eager parse vs progressive yield. Chosen: progressive yield with optional 'awaitComplete' helper for callers that need full objects
Compatibility note: for existing customers who use manual discriminator fields, provide a `registerLegacyDiscriminator` migration helper that maps old keys to normalized discriminators
Observability: emit structured debug events for discriminator discovery and hydration errors to integrate with Console tracing
Performance: use incremental JSON token scanning rather than naive JSON.parse on concatenated buffers to reduce GC pressure
